results.title: Linear vs Notion: Comparison and review (2026)
results.content:
Linear and Notion are designed for different types of teams and workflows, and there is no objective winner between the two of them. Notion is a versatile all-in-one workspace, while Linear is a specialized project management tool designed specifically for software development projects. Notion offers broad functionality across various domains, whereas Linear excels in providing a focused and streamlined solution tailored for software teams. [...] Unlike Notion, Linear is specifically tailored for software development projects. It provides a streamlined and focused approach to project tracking and collaboration within the software development context.

Linear stands out for its simplicity and efficiency, avoiding the all-encompassing features found in Notion. While Notion offers a broader range of functionalities, Linear zeroes in on the essentials for software development teams, offering a more targeted and purposeful tool. [...] — G2 review

### Notion

 Pricing: Free, advanced features starting from $10/user/month
 Rating on Capterra: 4.7/5

Notion is a versatile productivity tool that shares similarities with Linear but adopts a broader scope.

While Linear targets software development with a focus on Agile methodologies, Notion caters to a wider range of users and use cases. Notion's flexibility allows users to create databases, wikis, and knowledge bases, in addition to managing projects and tracking issues.

results.title: Linear vs. Notion: Which Is Right for Your Team?
results.content:
Linear is a specialized project management and issue tracking platform designed exclusively for software development teams, founded in 2019 and now serving over 25,000 companies including OpenAI, Coinbase, and Vercel. It positions itself as "the system for product development"—purpose-built for planning and building products in the AI era. The platform centralizes issue tracking, cycle (sprint) planning, project roadmaps, and real-time analytics in a single fast, keyboard-driven interface. [...] Notion is an AI-powered collaborative workspace platform that consolidates knowledge management, project management, and documentation into a single customizable system. It spans multiple categories — knowledge base, project tracking, and team docs — which reflects how broadly teams end up using it. Most adopt Notion to replace several disconnected tools at once.

Key Features: [...] Linear vs. Notion

Linear and Notion keep ending up on the same shortlist, but they're not competing for the same job. Linear is purpose-built for engineering teams that live in Git. Notion is a flexible workspace for teams that need docs, wikis, and lightweight project tracking in one place.

results.title: 3D-printing platform rapidly produces complex electric machines | MIT News | Massachusetts Institute of Technology
results.content:
Making a motor

After perfecting the printing platform, the researchers fabricated a linear motor, which generates straight-line motion (as opposed to a rotating motor, like the one in a car). Linear motors are used in applications like pick-and-place robotics, optical systems, and baggage conveyers. [...] The researchers used this system to produce a fully 3D-printed electric linear motor in a matter of hours using five materials. They only needed to perform one post-processing step for the motor to be fully functional.

The assembled device performed as well or better than similar motors that require more complex fabrication methods or additional post-processing steps. [...] ### Gizmodo

Researchers at MIT have developed a new 3D printing platform that can “produce a fully functioning linear motor in about three hours,” reports Justin Caffier for Gizmodo. The research team “explained how by retrofitting a printer with enough extruders to handle the various materials needed to make a working motor, they decimated the usual production time for such a device and brought the material costs down to around $0.50,” writes Caffier.

Source: © Johan Jamestad/The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences [...] Other researchers have also helped to expand chemists’ understanding of the mechanisms of non-linear effects and asymmetric autocatalysis.
